title: Kingfish club, small combo and tips at the Famous Door
summary: Harris recalls a four-piece combo with Smiling Joe, collecting tips, and generous gamblers at the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I've been selling the French market. The Black Cat, but by the old French market. That's what that job was playing.
I went with Smiling Joe. That's the thing I was trying to think of, Harry. What's the name of that club was by the French market? You had the Black Cat. Kingfish. Yeah, the Kingfish.
You remember when me and Smiling Joe, Elton, and Lil Woods? That's right. We had a four-piece combo. That's right.
That's right. I was playing at the Popeye. I was wearing those socks.

That's when them detectives used to come in and you asked for a tip to take the pistol and put it in the kitty. I said, I just can't. You can have the whole box. I don't know what that was. You see, at that time, well, the only way you make tips, it wouldn't come up to the bandstand like people do and put money in the kitty, you know? You'd have to take the box and walk around the tables and ask different people, you know, put something in the kitty. And that's the only way we could make little tips or something. They'd cover that week's salary. You didn't make no little tips.
You made no big tips. You made no big tips.
That's a cute fish. All right, you know.

And I'll tell you what, we did make a lot of big tips at the Famous Do. Famous Do. Yeah, we had this guy that owned the Louisine Coffee, Mr. Riley. He came in one night and gave us $20 a piece and he's playing, show me the way to go home. $20 a piece. And this guy used to own the South Pole when they had all that big gambling here. The South Pole, used to call him Big Diamond Jim or something. Used to have that big diamond pin up in his chest there. And each side of his pockets, nothing but big packs of money like that. That's what used to come. When he closed up, he'd come there and have all that money in his coat pockets. And each side pockets and all.
And Smiling Jewel would go by the table with his guitar. That's $50 right there. $50. Yeah. And then women just said, they were just snatched.
Yeah, but that fella's out at Spring there. They take care of musicians.

Yeah. Well, he's taking us down at the old Alpsen House where Pichon was playing. He's taking us down there and he give us $10 a piece. After he give us a $20. He gave us $10 a piece to go around and play one number with Fat Pichon. Fat Pichon. Fat Pichon said, he's glad you all came the other night there. I ain't did nothing if I give it. He give that $20. He was a nice poot. Them kind of guys was nice poot at that time. It was nothing. A $50 bill wasn't nothing from this. Why didn't they meet all that money in that gambling up there? You know what? He said, yeah. There's nothing from them coming. Just give it away. Yeah, well, make it easy.
